items.title: With FDA approval, Lilly’s BTK drug Jaypirca enters first-line CLL
items.summary: Eli Lilly’s Jaypirca, the first noncovalent BTK inhibitor, has won FDA approval for the first-line treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma, a market now led by BeOne’s Brukinsa.

items.title: Pfizer touts 'dermatology momentum' as it paints fuller picture of Litfulo's vitiligo potential
items.summary: Pfizer has detailed two clinical wins for its immunology portfolio as it aims for a label expansion, an approval and new indications beyond dermatology, too.

items.title: FDA hits 2nd Fresenius site with contamination-related warning letter in less than a month
items.summary: The agency raised concerns about contamination and quality control at Fresenius Kabi's Melrose Park facility in Illinois.

items.title: Hansoh’s Tagrisso rival loses EU approval after AstraZeneca legal challenge
items.summary: The European Commission has revoked the EU marketing authorization for Hansoh Pharma’s EGFR lung cancer drug Aumseqa following a legal challenge from rival AstraZeneca.

items.title: New EU supply chain to end Visudyne shortage

items.title: Abbott launches SimpleScreen CRC blood test in the US
items.summary: Abbott is kick-starting the U.S. commercial launch of SimpleScreen CRC, an FDA-approved blood-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening test for adults age 45 and older who are at average risk for the disease.

items.title: Patient death in BMS pulmonary fibrosis trial raises questions, but analysts unshaken
items.summary: The revelation of a patient death in Bristol Myers Squibb’s phase 3 trial of a potential pulmonary fibrosis treatment has raised concerns ahead of the study’s readout, but analysts were quick to dispel worries about broader implications for the drug mechanism involved.

items.title: Biopharma recruiters see ‘signs of recovery’ as layoffs remain cool in Q3’26
items.summary: A more subdued volume of biopharma layoffs continued into the third quarter of 2026, validating predictions that the sector has moved beyond the avalanche of redundancies experienced last year.

items.title: Zealand's stock slides as Boehringer-partnered obesity drug underwhelms again in phase 3
items.summary: A phase 3 trial of Boehringer Ingelheim’s survodutide in people with obesity and Type 2 diabetes has met its co-primary endpoints. Yet, with the readout echoing earlier data that underwhelmed analysts, shares in Boehringer’s partner Zealand Pharma fell 12% in early trading in Denmark.

items.title: Connect’s Dupixent rival reduces COPD attacks by 85%, but misses a secondary goal
items.summary: Connect Biopharma has pointed to phase 2 data for its IL-4/IL-13 blocker as proof that the wannabe Dupixent rival can reduce respiratory attacks—although the study missed a secondary endpoint tied to a breathing test.

items.title: VertigoDx on firm ground with FDA greenlight for vertigo diagnostic system
items.summary: The FDA has granted 510(k) clearance to Miami-based VertigoDx for its portable diagnostic system that can evaluate vertigo, including benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPVV).

items.title: Roche, Zealand see phase 2 amylin weight loss peak at mid-dose, start pivotal program
items.summary: Zealand Pharma has shared primary endpoint data on Roche-partnered petrelintide, revealing that the middle dose of the amylin analog delivered the highest weight loss—9.8%—at Week 28.

items.title: Lilly sets up next-gen obesity battle with full phase 3 retatrutide data
items.summary: Eli Lilly has shared detailed data from a phase 3 retatrutide trial, revealing that more than one-third of patients on the top dose of the triple-G drug candidate lost at least 25% of their body weight.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: FDA green lights Camzyos in kids; J&J blocks Simponi biosimilars
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: Lilly gives deeper glimpse at Foundayo's heart-helping odds in diabetes, obesity phase 3
items.summary: In a new update, Lilly tied Foundayo to a 53% reduction in the risk of cardiovascular death and a 57% lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with insulin glargine in a preplanned analysis of its phase 3 Achieve-4 trial.

items.title: Taiho scores phase 3 win with oral cancer combo for AML-causing blood disorders
items.summary: The oral combination treatment delivered the same exposure to azacitidine as when the chemo was given subcutaneously—meeting Taiho’s primary endpoint.

items.title: Vanda lines up new expansion prospect for Hetlioz as FDA jet lag hearing looms
items.summary: As Vanda Pharmaceuticals awaits a long-sought hearing with the FDA around a potential Hetlioz label expansion into jet lag disorder, the melatonin receptor agonist has demonstrated its merit in another sleep indication with a current dearth of treatment options.

items.title: BioMarin lays off 117 California workers to consolidate footprint
items.summary: Just months after trimming jobs in New Jersey following an acquisition, BioMarin is laying off 117 employees in California as part of a consolidation of its footprint.

items.title: ‘We’ve been taking our time’: Buzzy AI biotech Xaira reveals antibody platform, first taste of pipeline
items.summary: When Xaira Therapeutics first debuted in 2024 with a gobsmacking $1 billion in funding, a natural expectation would have been for a flurry of further activity to follow. Instead, the buzzy AI biotech went quiet.

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—Bayer taps new chief medical officer; Cantor appointed PhRMA CEO
items.summary: Eric Cantor, who represented Virginia in the U.S. House of Representatives for 14 years and served as House majority leader from 2011 to 2014, will step up as PhRMA’s next president and CEO on Nov. 9. Plus, Bayer has a new chief medical officer.

items.title: Novartis pens $7.8B deal for Abogen's in vivo autoimmune T-cell engager
items.summary: Novartis is paying Abogen Biosciences $575 million upfront for an mRNA-encoded T-cell engager that showed early clinical promise in autoimmune disease. The deal, which includes up to $7.2 billion in milestones, comes weeks after Novartis paused an autoimmune CAR-T program over three deaths.

items.title: Immunotherapy startup Adecto blames ‘risk-averse funding environment’ for closing down
items.summary: Adecto Pharmaceuticals’ 12-year story has come to an end as the immunotherapy biotech blamed a “risk-averse funding environment” for shutting up shop.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Foghorn cuts workforce by 40%; BioMarin drops 117 roles
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: Roche launches simultaneous screening test for SMA, SCID and SCD
items.summary: Roche Diagnostics has launched a new in vitro diagnostic test for newborn screening to detect a series of rare disorders.

items.title: Foghorn lays off 40% of employees as Lilly cancer collab collapses over poor data
items.summary: Foghorn Therapeutics is laying off 40% of its workforce after a long-running collaboration with Eli Lilly collapsed over disappointing phase 1 data.

items.title: ‘We’re so close to the tech companies’: Genentech CEO talks Fierce through vision for the future
items.summary: When recombinant DNA pioneer Herbert Boyer, Ph.D., first got a call from venture capitalist Robert Swanson about starting a company, the savvy scientist wasn’t sure a meeting would be worth his time.

items.title: Sanofi pays Dupixent partner Regeneron $1B upfront for 4 early-stage assets to ignite R&D
items.summary: Sanofi is paying Regeneron $1 billion upfront to collaborate on four early-stage immunology programs, teeing the longstanding partners up to try to replicate Dupixent’s success.

items.title: Lilly raises diabetes weight-loss bar with amylin-Zepbound combo
items.summary: Eli Lilly announced its amylin-Zepbound combination eloraTZP resulted in 23.3% weight loss in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight, topping its own triple-G drug candidate retatrutide in that population.

items.title: Beam Therapeutics sues base editing rival, claims former scientist stole secrets
items.summary: Base editing biotech Beam Therapeutics is suing one of its newest rivals, alleging that the upstart company stole the secrets behind one of its lead programs and used them to craft a competing therapy.

items.title: Merck’s anti-TL1A antibody secures a win in ph. 2 hidradenitis suppurativa trial
items.summary: Merck & Co. touted a win for its anti-TL1A antibody in a phase 2b trial in patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).

items.title: Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker '26: TriGemX tacks on $94M; AnaCardio adds $71M
items.summary: The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.
